description: Build a Streamlit app that generates a daily list of 30 prioritized, optimally routed stores per GCU for field agents, replacing manual store selection with a scored, ranked, and routed daily plan.

userStories.title: Data loading + filtering pipeline
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a data loading module that reads the store leads CSV, parses all date columns, and filters out ineligible stores before any scoring happens.
acceptanceCriteria: Load '[Growth]_Resat_Store_Leads_3.0_v2_2026_05_20.csv' into a pandas DataFrame
Parse 'last_delivered_date' and 'visit_date' as datetime columns (errors='coerce')
Exclude stores where 'latest_order_status' is 'pending' or 'dispatched'
Exclude stores where 'bakit hindi umorder si customer?' contains 'Permanently Closed', 'Temporarily Closed', or 'Wala ang may ari'
Exclude stores where 'visit_date' is within the last 7 days
Function returns a clean filtered DataFrame
GitHub issue #1 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Pool splitter — New/Revival vs P30D
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a pool splitter that divides filtered stores into two named pools per GCU based on last_delivered_date.
acceptanceCriteria: Stores with 'last_delivered_date' 60+ days ago OR null (never ordered) go into the New/Revival pool
Stores with 'last_delivered_date' 31–60 days ago go into the P30D pool
Pools are scoped per GCU — function accepts a GCU code and returns two DataFrames
Both pools exclude stores already excluded by the filter pipeline
GitHub issue #2 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Store scoring engine
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a scoring engine that normalizes all inputs and applies weighted formulas to rank stores within each pool.
acceptanceCriteria: All numeric inputs are min-max normalized to [0, 1] per pool before weighting (use +1e-9 in denominator to handle zero-range edge case)
New/Revival scoring: 0.30 × days_since_last_delivered + 0.25 × churn_tier + 0.20 × never_visited_bonus + 0.15 × geographic_cluster_density + 0.05 × delivery_proximity_score + 0.05 × attempt_penalty
churn_tier: 2=never ordered (null last_delivered_date), 1=60+ days churned, 0=approaching 60 days
never_visited_bonus: 1 if number_of_visits == 0 or null, else 0
geographic_cluster_density: count of other eligible stores within 2km radius using haversine distance
delivery_proximity_score: computed from 'delivery_days' column — score = max(0, (7 - days_until_next_delivery) / 6), where 1 day away = 1.0, 7 days away = 0.0
attempt_penalty: normalized number_of_visits (higher visits = higher penalty, subtracted from score)
P30D scoring: 0.30 × no_delivered_orders + 0.30 × days_since_last_delivered + 0.25 × delivery_proximity_score + 0.15 × recency_of_drop_off
Each store has a final 'score' column between 0 and 1
Stores are sorted descending by score within each pool
GitHub issue #3 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Store selector — 70:30 split with cross-pool backfill
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a store selector that picks exactly 30 stores per GCU using the 70:30 split, with automatic backfill when a pool runs short.
acceptanceCriteria: Default split: top 21 from New/Revival pool + top 9 from P30D pool
If New/Revival has fewer than 21 stores, take all available and backfill remainder from P30D
If P30D has fewer than 9 stores, take all available and backfill remainder from New/Revival
Output is always exactly 30 stores (or all eligible stores if fewer than 30 exist in the GCU)
No duplicate stores in the final selection
Output DataFrame includes a 'pool' column indicating 'New/Revival' or 'P30D' for each store
GitHub issue #4 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Route optimizer — nearest-neighbor from GCU centroid
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a route optimizer that orders the 30 selected stores using a nearest-neighbor heuristic starting from the GCU centroid.
acceptanceCriteria: GCU centroid is computed as mean lat/long of all eligible stores in the GCU (not just the 30 selected)
Nearest-neighbor traversal starts from the centroid and visits each of the 30 stores exactly once
Uses haversine distance for all proximity calculations
Output is the 30 stores as an ordered DataFrame with a 'rank' column (1–30)
GitHub issue #5 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Streamlit app shell — GCU selector + generate pipeline
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want a Streamlit app where I can select a GCU and generate the daily store list by clicking a button.
acceptanceCriteria: App file is named app.py and runs with 'streamlit run app.py'
Store data loads from CSV on startup using @st.cache_data
GCU dropdown lists all unique GCU codes derived from the data
Clicking 'Generate List' runs the full pipeline: filter → split → score → select → route
Resulting 30 ordered stores are stored in st.session_state['daily_list']
A success message shows the GCU name and store count after generation
GitHub issue #6 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Folium map — numbered pins + route line
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want to see the 30 stores plotted on a map with numbered markers and a route line connecting them in visit order.
acceptanceCriteria: Map is rendered using folium and embedded via streamlit-folium (st_folium)
Map centers on the GCU centroid at zoom level 13
Each store is shown as a numbered marker (1–30) in visit order
A blue polyline connects the stores in visit order
Hovering or clicking a marker shows the store name and barangay
Map only renders after 'Generate List' is clicked
GitHub issue #7 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Store table — ordered visit list below map
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want to see a table below the map showing the 30 stores in visit order with key details.
acceptanceCriteria: Table appears below the map after list generation
Columns: Rank, Store Name, Barangay, City, Pool (New/Revival or P30D), Days Since Last Order
'Days Since Last Order' shows an integer (today minus last_delivered_date), or 'Never' if null
Rows are sorted by rank ascending (rank 1 at top)
Rendered with st.dataframe with a fixed height of 400px
GitHub issue #8 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: CSV export per GCU
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want to download the 30-store list as a CSV to simulate the CASA push.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Download CSV' button appears after list generation
CSV columns: rank, store_name, barangay, city, gcu, lat, long, last_delivered_date, no_delivered_orders, delivery_days, pool
Stores are in visit order (rank 1 first)
File is named '{gcu}_daily_list.csv' (e.g., 'CB01_daily_list.csv')
Implemented with st.download_button — no server-side file writing
GitHub issue #9 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Streamlit Cloud deployment
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want the app deployed to a public URL so leadership can access it for the demo.
acceptanceCriteria: App is deployed to Streamlit Cloud from the AndrewMarasigan31/agent-compliance-hackathon GitHub repo
CSV data file is committed to the repo so the deployed app can load it
Public URL is accessible without login
Selecting a GCU and generating a list works end-to-end on the deployed app

userStories.title: Geographic clustering for beat generation
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want beats to be geographically contiguous so agents cover one zone per day without criss-crossing the GCU.
acceptanceCriteria: Number of beats (K) is computed as ceil(eligible_store_count / 30) per GCU
K-means clusters stores by lat/long into K geographic zones using sklearn KMeans
Each zone becomes one beat — stores within the zone are sorted by score descending, then routed via nearest-neighbor
Each beat is ranked 1–30 (or 1–N for the last beat if stores don't divide evenly into 30)
No store appears in more than one beat
The 70:30 New/Revival vs P30D split is preserved within each zone's scoring
All-beats map view shows geographically contiguous zones with no crossing routes
Existing UI (beat selector, toggle, table, CSV export) works unchanged
GitHub issue #11 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Geography-first beat generation across all GCUs
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want beats generated from global geographic clustering across all stores regardless of GCU boundaries, so agents visit stores that are physically close together.
acceptanceCriteria: All eligible stores across all GCUs are clustered together by lat/long using K-means, where K = ceil(total eligible stores / 30)
Each cluster becomes one beat — stores within the cluster are scored with 70:30 split applied, then routed via nearest-neighbor
Each beat is ranked 1–30 (or 1–N for the last beat)
No store appears in more than one beat
UI removes the GCU dropdown — replaced with a single 'Generate All Beats' button
Beat selector dropdown (Beat 1, Beat 2, ...) lets supervisor browse all beats
Each beat's map, table, and CSV export work unchanged
'Show all beats' toggle shows all geographic clusters on one map with distinct colors
GitHub issue #12 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Scoring system overhaul — recency-first with hard exclusions
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want the scoring system to prioritize recently churned stores (warmer leads) and exclude stores that have repeatedly failed to convert.
acceptanceCriteria: Exclude stores with number_of_visits >= 5 AND no_delivered_orders == 0 before scoring
New/Revival pool capped at 60–365 days churned — exclude stores churned more than 365 days ago (never-ordered stores still included)
New/Revival formula: 0.35 × never_visited + 0.30 × (1 - n_days) + 0.20 × cluster_density + 0.15 × delivery_proximity
churn_tier and attempt_penalty factors removed from New/Revival scoring
days_since direction flipped for New/Revival — lower days = higher score
P30D formula: 0.40 × order_frequency + 0.35 × delivery_proximity + 0.25 × (1 - n_days)
n_recency removed from P30D scoring
All existing UI (beat selector, map, table, CSV export) works unchanged
GitHub issue #13 closed with comment linking to the commit

userStories.title: Last delivered date year filter for New/Revival pool
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want to control how far back the app looks for churned stores by selecting a cutoff year, so I can include older leads when needed.
acceptanceCriteria: Year dropdown appears after CSV upload, before the Generate All Beats button
Options are dynamically derived from unique years in uploaded CSV's last_delivered_date column, sorted descending, plus 'All time' as the last option
Default selection is the year equivalent to 730 days ago from today
Selecting a year filters New/Revival pool to last_delivered_date >= Jan 1 of selected year
P30D pool (31–60 days) is unaffected by the year filter
Never-ordered stores (null last_delivered_date) are always included regardless of year filter
Selection is persisted in st.session_state alongside nr_ratio and agent_name
Existing CLOSED_REASONS exclusions (Permanently Closed, Temporarily Closed, Masikip ang Daan, Duplicate Account) remain unchanged
GitHub issue #14 closed with comment linking to the commit
